subject: Sandbox deployment SLA — uptime floor & monthly remedy split
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@sandboxco.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@sandboxco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sandbox SLA proposal — baseline & remedy structure

Hi Megan / Tom,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — appreciated the clarity on your sandbox usage patterns. As promised, attaching a first pass SLA tailored for the sandbox environment and how we'd treat uptime vs monthly remedies (attached: sandbox-sla-draft-v1.pdf). Key highlights: 

- Baseline uptime: 99.5% for sandbox tenants (production remains 99.9% in our standard T&Cs).
- Remedy model: monthly service credits for sandbox are scaled (see table in doc) — starting at 5% credit for 99.0–99.4% and increasing to 25% for <98.0%.
- Cap: credits for sandbox limited to 50% of monthly sandbox invoice; production accounts retain the standard 100% cap.
- Maintenance carve-outs: scheduled maint windows (up to 6 hours/month) excluded from uptime calculations when notified 72 hours in advance.

We recommended the lower uptime floor for sandbox because the workload is expected to tolerate more variance and it lets us offer a more flexible pricing/seat model while keeping the production SLA tight. That said, happy to adjust thresholds or cap if SandboxCo needs tighter guarantees for certain pilot clusters.

Next steps: if the structure looks directionally right, can Ben and I iterate a v2 and we can loop in Legal for a redline.

Thanks,
Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sandbox-sla-draft-v1.pdf, uptime-metrics-chart.png
From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@sandboxco.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@sandboxco.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sandbox SLA proposal — baseline & remedy structure

Sergio — thanks for the quick turnaround and the doc. Tom and I reviewed with the platform team. A few clarifying questions / asks before we go to legal: 

1) Sandbox pods are customer-facing for our beta users; can we move the sandbox uptime floor to 99.7% for named pilot clusters (we have ~4 clusters total)?
2) For credits, can the monthly cap be 75% of sandbox invoice (instead of 50%) for the pilot clusters only?
3) Would Redwood consider a hard floor for monthly latency p95 for sandbox (e.g., <300ms) tied to a smaller credit bucket — our QA tooling flags regressions otherwise.

Also — what's the expected notification cadence for scheduled maintenance? 72 hours is fine, but during the pilot we'll need to limit maintenance during peak beta hours (weeknights 18:00–22:00 PT).

If you can propose a counter that separates "named pilot clusters" from general sandbox tenancy, that would help us justify internally.

Best,
Megan
Head of Platform Partnerships
SandboxCo
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan.liu@sandboxco.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@sandboxco.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Sandbox SLA proposal — baseline & remedy structure

Megan — appreciate the specifics. Sergio and I discussed and put together a counterproposal that creates two buckets (attached: sandbox-sla-draft-v2.pdf):

A) Named pilot clusters (up to 4 clusters) — elevated sandbox SLA: 99.7% uptime, credits scaled but capped at 75% of the sandbox invoice for those clusters. Latency: p95 < 300ms commitment; credits for latency regressions are smaller (1–5% bands) and applied separately from uptime credits.

B) General sandbox tenancy — baseline: 99.5% uptime and 50% monthly credit cap (as originally proposed).

Other points: 
- Maintenance windows: we can commit to avoiding planned maints for named pilot clusters during your stated peak hours. Emergency maints still have to be covered under the carve-outs but we'll provide notification as early as possible and aim for rollback plans.
- Measurement & reporting: we'll provide a shared dashboard (view-only link) and monthly CSV export with uptime and p95 latency by cluster.
- Legal redline: if you sign off on the two-bucket approach I can fast-track a redline with Laura (legal) and aim for a pilot addendum rather than a full contract amendment.

Would you like us to convert the pilot clusters into a separate line item on invoices so the cap and credits apply cleanly? That also makes reconciliations faster.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sandbox-sla-draft-v2.pdf
From: Megan Liu <megan.liu@sandboxco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@sandboxco.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sandbox SLA proposal — baseline & remedy structure

Ben / Sergio — thanks, the two-bucket approach addresses our main concerns. Two quick asks before we route to procurement/legal: 

- Please add a line in the v2 that the pilot-cluster invoice line will be clearly labeled and that credits are calculable per-cluster.
- Add an explicit one-month review clause after pilot launch to revisit p95 latency banding if we see systematic variance.

If you add those two bullets we can get Procurement to start a redline next week — Tom will share procurement contact details in a separate note.

Appreciate the rapid iteration.

Best,
Megan
Head of Platform Partnerships
SandboxCo
